name: Hue Citadel
kicker: Walled imperial court on the north bank
summary: Give the morning to the Imperial City, the walled court inside the citadel, on a 200,000 VND adult ticket. The tombs are not on that ticket. Walk in from the south bank at opening, 06:30 or 07:00, and confirm the board because the hours page did not reload.
getThere: Walk from the south bank. Minutes are Check on arrival.
heroCaption: Ngọ Môn, the king's gate, from the front

notice.title: The 200,000 VND ticket is the Imperial City only
notice.body: Minh Mang, Tu Duc, and Khai Dinh are separate tickets, or the four-site ticket at 530,000 VND for an adult and 100,000 VND for a child from 7 to 12, usable for up to two days from the first visit. The royal antiquities museum, An Dinh, Hon Chen, and Nam Giao are other lines on the same resolution. Thien Mu is not on it.

body: Enter at the ticketed Imperial City. The centre describes the outer citadel as about 10 km around, with walls about 6.6 m high, and the Imperial City inside it at about 600 m a side. Ngọ Môn was the king’s gate. Beyond it the courts run to the Thái Hòa palace, the ancestral temples, and the Forbidden Purple City, built in 1804, with the Duyệt Thị Đường theatre.

Buy the ticket for the courts you will actually walk. The 200,000 VND adult price is the Imperial City. It is the same for an international visitor and a Vietnamese visitor. A child from 7 to 12 pays 40,000 VND, and a child under 7 is free. Hue residents and the other groups named in Resolution 55 pay half.

Go at opening. The centre’s notice of 12 March 2024 says 06:30 from 16 March to 15 October, with tickets until 17:30, and 07:00 from 16 October to 15 March, with tickets until 17:00. A direct reload of that page timed out on 21 October 2026, so confirm the board. No weekly closing day is on the notice. How long the courts take is Check on arrival. The ticket site names an audio guide and an electric cart, with phone numbers and no prices.

figures.caption: Thái Hòa palace across the water, inside the Imperial City
figures.alt: The yellow-roofed Thái Hòa palace seen across a pool from a painted gate inside the Hue Imperial City

gettingThere: The Imperial City sits on the north bank, inside the outer citadel. Walk from the south bank. Phu Xuan Bridge is the crossing the culture department names. Truong Tien Bridge is the other, at the start of the river path from the bridge to Nghinh Luong Dinh. The minutes are Check on arrival.

legs.heading: From the south bank
legs.body: Walk across Phu Xuan Bridge or Truong Tien Bridge. No published minute count from a hotel street. Check on arrival.

hours: 16 Mar–15 Oct: 06:30–18:00, tickets until 17:30. 16 Oct–15 Mar: 07:00–17:30, tickets until 17:00. Confirm on arrival. The source is the centre’s 12 Mar 2024 notice, and a direct reload timed out on 21 Oct 2026.
closed: No weekly closing day is on that notice. Confirm the board on arrival.
admissionNote: Adult 200,000 VND, the same price for an international visitor and a Vietnamese visitor. A child from 7 to 12 pays 40,000 VND. Under 7 is free. Hue residents and the other groups named in Resolution 55/2025/NQ-HĐND pay half. The ticket is the Imperial City only. The four-site ticket, Imperial City plus Minh Mang, Tu Duc, and Khai Dinh, is 530,000 VND for an adult and 100,000 VND for a child from 7 to 12, for up to two days from the first visit. An audio guide and an electric cart are named on the ticket site, with no prices. Those prices are Check on arrival.
